To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

relative intrinsic exercise goal content was positively associated with physical self-worth and psychological need satisfaction, and was negatively associated with exercise anxiety, after controlling for relative autonomous exercise motivation.
relative intrinsic goal content was related to positive cognitive, affective and behavioral outcomes and that this relationship was partially mediated by psychological need satisfaction.
relative intrinsic exercise goals are associated with positive outcomes (e.g., physical self-worth) and that this association is partly mediated by psychological need satisfaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of exercise goals in the promotion of physical and psychological well-being.
the motivational underpinnings of exercise behavior, specifically, the goal content of individuals’ exercise goals and its relationship to exercise outcomes.
the role of exercise goal content in predicting exercise outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the current study support the goal content perspective of SDT, which suggests that the content of exercise goals is more predictive of psychological need satisfaction and psychological well-being than the relative self-determination of those exercise goals.
the results of this study support the notion that relative intrinsic goal content is associated with positive cognitive, affective and behavioural outcomes.
the more participants reported intrinsic exercise goal content, the more positive their outcomes and the less negative they were.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

intrinsic goals are associated with more beneficial exercise outcomes, including greater psychological need satisfaction, and that psychological need satisfaction partially mediates the effect of intrinsic goals on exercise outcomes.
the content of exercise goals matters, and that relative intrinsic goals may be particularly important for promoting positive outcomes and reducing negative outcomes.

the more an individual’s exercise goal content is comprised of intrinsic goals, the more positive the cognitive, affective and behavioral outcomes will be, as well as the more satisfied their psychological needs will be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the content of one’s exercise goals is a critical factor in understanding the psychological benefits and behavioral consequences associated with exercise.
exercise goals that are more intrinsic in nature may be beneficial to the exercise behavior and well-being of exercisers.
exercise goals should be conceptualized and measured with a focus on their content, rather than their source.
